A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ResFormer/SVFormer research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SlimPajama training experiments, zero-shot downstream accuracies, ablations, representation analyses, and appendix validation losses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds validation-scaling analyses, residual-weight sweeps, and attention-concentration diagnostics.

M1.justification: The principal ResFormer and SVFormer procedures remain unchanged in Equations 7 and 10. However, v3 Section 4.2 introduces and tests the weighted variant U_n = A_n(V_n + lambda V_1), a limited procedural extension that changes residual weighting and scaling.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven-domain SlimPajama mixture, six commonsense reasoning tasks, and Llama/Mistral models for analysis. Sequence-length coverage is retained. New model configurations and diagnostics do not expand the represented data domains or task requirements.

E2.justification: SVFormer joins the existing trained-model entropy comparison in v3 Figure 1, and full cross-layer attention participates in the new 82M diagnostics in Figure 20. DenseFormer/NeuTRENO training comparisons and GQA/CLA cache comparisons remain. The mapping-ablation labels 'Gold Attention' and 'Cross Layer Attention' refer to the retained Equation 2 comparator.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands efficiency and mechanism evaluation: displayed model-size scaling changes from training loss to validation loss, adds a 320M configuration, and evaluates 468M checkpoints every 2B tokens. It also introduces randomly initialized controls, coefficient sweeps, and token-importance/state-norm measurements. The main pretraining budget and downstream zero-shot protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds ResFormer and NeuTRENO coefficient-sensitivity studies, an initialization control separating concentration from over-smoothing, and extensive first-token, state-norm, and importance-distribution analyses (Figures 1–2, 8, 19–22). Conversely, v1's trained-model token-similarity comparison and model-size training-curve panels are removed or replaced by validation-scaling analyses. Most original component and sharing ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report smoothed training curves and averages over examples. Neither supplies training-seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added analyses do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds scaling estimates of 10.4% fewer parameters and 13.6% less training data for ResFormer, and 12.2% more parameters for SVFormer, at equivalent Transformer validation loss (Figures 6 and 15d). It adds sensitivity and state-norm findings and removes earlier training-size and token-similarity results. Trained-model entropy curves also change substantially without clear setting reconciliation. Tables 1 and 5 remain numerically identical.

T1.justification: Equation 8 changes NeuTRENO's subtraction operator from lambda times an explicitly defined all-ones matrix J to lambda times the identity matrix I. This corrects a substantive mathematical distinction, consistent with the described value-vector difference. The central cross-layer approximation derivation remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the two-method contribution but shift emphasis from broad superiority and faster training to quantified validation-efficiency benefits and an explicit SVFormer parameter penalty. They also elevate avoidance of value-state drains, including SVFormer's mitigation of concentration, into central claims.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes architectural over-smoothing from attention concentration emerging during training and proposes disruption of value-drain feedback as ResFormer's mechanism. Appendix A.1 weakens the earlier causal conclusion to correlation. The revision also limits SVFormer's speed advantage to early training and replaces model-size insensitivity language with an explicit capacity-cost tradeoff.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies lambda = 0.2 for combined ResFormer/NeuTRENO, while retaining standalone lambda = 0.4 and most implementation tables. It removes explicit entropy-sample length and downstream model-size disclosures. Its reproducibility statement changes from already released code to a future release, conflicting with the retained code-available footnote; actual availability is unresolved by the PDFs.

R1.justification: New Darcet, two Guo, and Sun references, together with expanded discussion of the retained attention-sinks work, substantially reposition the paper around registers, attention biases, value-state drains, and activation peaks. Novelty is situated in cross-layer concentration patterns and indirect mitigation. Bibliographic publication updates alone do not account for this change.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introduction/results passages are rewritten, two analytical appendix subsections are inserted, and acknowledgements are removed. The main section sequence and much existing prose remain intact. Local editing also introduces the erroneous 'ResFormer ... lower final loss than ResFormer' sentence in Section 4.3.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: Figure 1 is recomposed and moved onto the first page, existing plots are regrouped or wrapped into text, and new scaling, sensitivity, norm, and heatmap displays are added. Only the pretrained-model half of v1 Figure 15 survives as v3 Figure 18. Existing tables are largely relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the paper's central explanation through initialization controls, state-norm diagnostics, and sensitivity evidence that v1 lacked. Validation-scaling analyses also make the efficiency benefits and SVFormer tradeoff more assessable, beyond v1's training-curve emphasis and retained validation table. These gains outweigh localized regressions, including conflicting code-release statements and an erroneous comparison sentence. Unexplained entropy-scale changes still limit confidence in that particular comparison.
